title: Directive on Public Service Information Security
summary: Turn the 2022 Directive into assigned, operating departmental controls and an improvement programme.
outcomes: Interpret the Directive in the departmental context.
Translate requirements into controls with evidence.
Manage access, change and supplier exceptions through accountable decisions.

realExample.title: DPSA reports implementation of government ICT norms
realExample.documentedOutcome: DPSA's 23 November 2023 progress report described implementation of public-service ICT norms, including information-security, cloud and governance instruments.
realExample.discussion: A national instrument becomes useful when departments assign the work, operate controls and resolve gaps. Trace one requirement from the issued instrument to the evidence a service owner would need.
realExample.scope: Documented policy implementation work; departmental effectiveness must be assessed separately.

units.title: From a directive clause to an operating control

chapters.title: Read the requirement in context
chapters.bodyHtml:
Read the Directive's purpose, scope and role provisions before extracting individual controls. The Head of Department's responsibility for departmental policy, the delegated DISO function and the GITO relationship form part of the implementation context. The ICT steering committee also provides a forum for security governance.

A requirement is not implemented simply because its wording appears in a local policy. Translate it into the relevant service process: who acts, on what trigger, using which authority, and what record remains. Check whether an existing process already meets it before creating a duplicate.

Keep the original clause reference next to the local interpretation. If a department uses different role titles, document the actual delegation rather than replacing the source wording without explanation. Where scope is uncertain, resolve the question through the responsible policy and legal roles.

chapters.title: A practical control map
chapters.bodyHtml:
Use six fields: source requirement, service scope, control objective, responsible owner, operating procedure and evidence. For access removal, the objective is that a person's access no longer exceeds an authorised need. The process may join HR departure notices, service-owner decisions, ICT changes and supplier confirmation.

Evidence should address the objective. A procedure demonstrates design. A dated removal record demonstrates an action. A comparison against the actual remaining accounts helps establish whether the removal covered the service. These are different claims; retain their scope.

Start with controls that protect important decisions and services. A useful map identifies gaps and action owners, not merely green ticks. Explain exclusions, dependencies and sampling limits so an executive can understand what the assurance does and does not cover.

chapters.title: Build an improvement programme that closes gaps
chapters.bodyHtml:
Group findings by the underlying service problem. Ten orphaned accounts caused by one broken HR-to-ICT notification process may require a single joined process improvement plus correction of the existing accounts. Treating each as an isolated ticket can leave the cause unchanged.

Prioritise by consequence, exposure and available temporary protection. Assign an owner with the ability to deliver, a due date, dependencies and a clear completion condition. Link the work to the departmental risk and governance programme.

Revisit the control after an important service or supplier change. An access review that was sufficient for read-only records may no longer cover a new payment-edit function. Implementation is an ongoing operating responsibility rather than an annual act of policy publication.

application.title: Create a clause-to-control implementation map
application.instructionsHtml:
Fictional case: a department has the Directive on its intranet but cannot show who reviews supplier access, how leavers are removed or whether a restored backup supports the current service.

Spend about 60 minutes preparing a five-row control map covering governance, access, awareness, change and recovery. For each, name a source provision area, local owner, procedure and useful evidence.
application.deliverable: A five-row implementation map and prioritised three-action plan.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Separate the existence of policy from its operation. For supplier access, show authorised users and current permissions; for leavers, reconcile actual accounts; for backups, require an observed recovery outcome.

Join related causes into a deliverable improvement. A single coordinated leaver process can address HR, internal systems and suppliers without creating parallel unowned registers.

Use the current Directive's exact clause numbers during departmental adoption and record any local interpretation explicitly.

reflection.prompt: Which local 'compliant' label currently rests only on a document's existence?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Identify one observation that would establish whether its control actually operates.

quiz.title: From a directive clause to an operating control — knowledge check

questions.name: M03-U01-Q01
questions.promptHtml: What should precede a clause checklist?

answers.textHtml: Reading the Directive's scope and roles
answers.feedbackHtml: Implementation starts with authority and context.

answers.textHtml: Selecting an implementation package before establishing applicability
answers.feedbackHtml: Product selection follows the actual scope and responsibilities.

answers.textHtml: Copying another institution's checklist without comparing its roles or services
answers.feedbackHtml: A reused checklist still needs an applicability assessment.

answers.textHtml: Assigning local job titles without mapping them to the source responsibilities
answers.feedbackHtml: The mapping must preserve the Directive's actual roles.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Implementation starts with authority and context.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q02
questions.promptHtml: Which evidence addresses whether a leaver's access was removed?

answers.textHtml: A check of remaining actual permissions against the authorised end state
answers.feedbackHtml: Compare the control outcome with the required state.

answers.textHtml: A helpdesk ticket marked closed without checking residual permissions
answers.feedbackHtml: Closure of a task record does not establish the actual access end state.

answers.textHtml: An HR termination notice with no downstream access confirmation
answers.feedbackHtml: The notice is an input to removal, not proof that all permissions were removed.

answers.textHtml: The administrator's description of the usual leaver procedure
answers.feedbackHtml: The normal design does not demonstrate what happened for this leaver.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Compare the control outcome with the required state.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q03
questions.promptHtml: Ten orphaned accounts share a broken HR notification cause. What is the strongest improvement?

answers.textHtml: Correct the accounts and repair the joined notification process
answers.feedbackHtml: Address current exposure and the recurring cause.

answers.textHtml: Correct the ten accounts but leave the broken HR trigger unchanged
answers.feedbackHtml: The same cause can create further orphaned accounts.

answers.textHtml: Replace the HR policy wording without joining the actual notification and access actions
answers.feedbackHtml: A policy edit alone does not repair the operating interface.

answers.textHtml: Ask each system administrator to guess which staff have left
answers.feedbackHtml: An informal guess is not a reliable joined leaver process.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Address current exposure and the recurring cause.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q04
questions.promptHtml: What does a written procedure primarily demonstrate?

answers.textHtml: Control design
answers.feedbackHtml: Design, execution and effectiveness are distinct.

answers.textHtml: That the control operated successfully for every relevant case
answers.feedbackHtml: A written procedure describes design, not every execution.

answers.textHtml: That the control achieved its intended service result
answers.feedbackHtml: Effectiveness requires relevant operating evidence.

answers.textHtml: That every supplier has implemented the same procedure
answers.feedbackHtml: A document does not establish external implementation.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Design, execution and effectiveness are distinct.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q05
questions.promptHtml: A local role title differs from the Directive. What should the map retain?

answers.textHtml: The source role and its actual local delegation
answers.feedbackHtml: Preserve the relationship between source authority and local implementation.

answers.textHtml: Only the local job title, omitting the source responsibility
answers.feedbackHtml: The map should preserve what the role is responsible for.

answers.textHtml: The assumption that a similar-sounding title has identical authority
answers.feedbackHtml: Actual delegation matters more than a label match.

answers.textHtml: A supplier's role chart used as the department's delegation
answers.feedbackHtml: External organisation does not establish departmental authority.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Preserve the relationship between source authority and local implementation.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q06
questions.promptHtml: Which change most clearly alters the risk assumptions of a read-only access review?

answers.textHtml: The service gains a payment-edit function
answers.feedbackHtml: Changed capability can change the risk and evidence needed.

answers.textHtml: A maintenance update confirmed to leave the permissions and information scope unchanged
answers.feedbackHtml: This does not by itself alter the review's stated access-risk assumptions.

answers.textHtml: A report template change that leaves the reviewed population and decisions unchanged
answers.feedbackHtml: A presentation change is different from a change in permitted actions.

answers.textHtml: A clarification to public help text with no change to service access
answers.feedbackHtml: The scenario does not introduce a new privileged function.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Changed capability can change the risk and evidence needed.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which fields make a control map useful? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Service scope and accountable owner
answers.feedbackHtml: These identify where and by whom it operates.

answers.textHtml: Procedure and outcome evidence
answers.feedbackHtml: These connect design to operation.

answers.textHtml: A green tick without supporting detail
answers.feedbackHtml: It hides the basis of the claim.

answers.textHtml: A vendor rank unrelated to the service
answers.feedbackHtml: It does not establish implementation.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A useful map supports decisions and follow-through.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which statements accurately describe implementation? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Existing processes can satisfy a requirement if their scope and operation fit
answers.feedbackHtml: Reuse can preserve accountability.

answers.textHtml: Gaps need owners and completion conditions
answers.feedbackHtml: This turns assessment into improvement.

answers.textHtml: Every clause requires a new separate system
answers.feedbackHtml: That creates unnecessary duplication.

answers.textHtml: Publishing a policy proves all controls work
answers.feedbackHtml: Operation requires additional evidence.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Implement requirements through coherent operating processes.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q09
questions.promptHtml: A control's sampled evidence should retain its scope and limitations.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Otherwise the conclusion can be broader than the observation.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Otherwise the conclusion can be broader than the observation.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Otherwise the conclusion can be broader than the observation.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q10
questions.promptHtml: The original clause reference can be discarded once a local checklist exists.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Source traceability is needed for interpretation and future changes.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: Source traceability is needed for interpretation and future changes.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Source traceability is needed for interpretation and future changes.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the evidence to its principal claim.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Each record supports a different stage of implementation.

questions.name: M03-U01-Q12
questions.promptHtml: A control map connects the source [[1]] to an operating [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The map bridges authority and daily work.

units.title: Access, change and supplier controls under pressure
objectives: Apply named access and review principles.
Govern urgent changes without losing accountability.
Specify supplier access and recovery requirements.

chapters.title: Access follows an authorised need
chapters.bodyHtml:
The Directive addresses personal user identities, access control and identity checking for password resets. In practice, access should be linked to a named person's approved role and current need. Joining, changing roles and leaving are distinct events; a transfer can require removal of old permissions as well as addition of new ones.

Review privileged and supplier access in the same service context. A supplier engineer's technical skill does not create a continuing right to every record. Confirm who approves the access, what it permits, when it ends and how activity can be examined.

A failed-login alert is information to assess, not proof of a malicious individual. Protect the service, verify identity through the approved route and retain useful facts. Avoid a shortcut in which a convincing phone caller receives a privileged reset without the required identity check.

chapters.title: Urgent change still needs a controlled decision
chapters.bodyHtml:
An urgent repair may be necessary to keep a public service operating. The Directive's change-management provisions address approval and control, including emergency changes. A useful emergency record identifies the service problem, proposed change, authority, risk, rollback or recovery plan and later review.

The approver needs to know the alternatives. A short controlled outage may be safer than an unreviewed database edit. Conversely, delaying an essential repair can itself harm the public. The decision should make both consequences visible.

After the change, verify the service outcome and reconcile any transactions processed during disruption. Preserve the actual configuration and decision record. Retrospective review should explain what happened and improve the normal process, rather than invent an approval that did not occur.

chapters.title: Suppliers, backups and continuing assurance
chapters.bodyHtml:
Third-party access needs a legitimate service purpose and an approved method. Include the personnel, technical access and information-handling responsibilities in the departmental relationship. Confirm who can revoke access and recover the service when support changes or the contract ends.

Backups are useful only when required information can be recovered in a usable condition. A successful copy job is one piece of evidence; a recovery exercise should also address the application, permissions, configuration and business reconciliation needed to resume the service.

Use recurring review to identify changes in the actual environment. New subcontractors, changed privilege, ageing recovery documentation and untested dependencies should become decisions with owners. Keep the review proportionate to service criticality and the applicable requirements.

application.title: Govern an urgent supplier repair
application.instructionsHtml:
A fictional benefits system fails during payment processing. A supplier proposes a direct production database edit using its shared account. Last night's backup completed, but nobody has restored the application with that backup. Payment-file generation may already have started.

Spend about 60 minutes drafting an emergency-change decision and the first post-change review agenda.
application.deliverable: One decision record, recovery checklist and follow-up action table.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Confirm the failure, transaction state, authorised change route and named access. Ask for a recoverable pre-change state and an alternative if the edit fails.

Assess whether payments were generated or sent before rerunning; avoid assuming a retry has no duplicate effect. Verify business records and service operation after the repair.

Record actual authority and times. Follow up shared access, restoration capability and the underlying defect; do not fabricate prior approval.

reflection.prompt: Which emergency workaround is most likely to become permanent in your department?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Propose an expiry, owner and completion condition that preserves the service while the cause is repaired.

quiz.title: Access, change and supplier controls under pressure — knowledge check

questions.name: M03-U02-Q01
questions.promptHtml: An employee transfers roles. What should access review consider?

answers.textHtml: Removal of old permissions and approval of new permissions
answers.feedbackHtml: Role changes require a complete view of authorised need.

answers.textHtml: Only adding the new permissions
answers.feedbackHtml: Old access can remain excessive.

answers.textHtml: Keeping every historical privilege forever
answers.feedbackHtml: Past need is not current authority.

answers.textHtml: Deleting all business records owned by the employee
answers.feedbackHtml: Access change is not records disposal.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Role changes require a complete view of authorised need.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q02
questions.promptHtml: A caller urgently requests an administrator password reset. What governs the response?

answers.textHtml: The approved identity-verification and reset process
answers.feedbackHtml: Verify identity before granting control.

answers.textHtml: Caller identification on a familiar phone number as the only identity check
answers.feedbackHtml: A familiar number alone may not meet the approved reset process.

answers.textHtml: A forwarded manager email accepted without the required identity verification
answers.feedbackHtml: A forwarded request does not replace the configured verification and authority steps.

answers.textHtml: Issuing the reset first and seeking routine approval afterwards
answers.feedbackHtml: Urgency does not by itself authorise bypassing the approved process.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Verify identity before granting control.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q03
questions.promptHtml: What distinguishes a controlled emergency change?

answers.textHtml: Explicit authority, risk, recovery plan and subsequent review
answers.feedbackHtml: An urgent decision can remain controlled and traceable.

answers.textHtml: No record because it was urgent
answers.feedbackHtml: Urgency increases the importance of clarity.

answers.textHtml: A fabricated earlier approval
answers.feedbackHtml: That corrupts the decision history.

answers.textHtml: Unrestricted supplier access indefinitely
answers.feedbackHtml: That exceeds the immediate need.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: An urgent decision can remain controlled and traceable.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q04
questions.promptHtml: A backup job says success. What remains to assess?

answers.textHtml: Whether the required service and information can actually be recovered
answers.feedbackHtml: Recovery includes data, application dependencies and business usability.

answers.textHtml: Only that the scheduled copy operation reported completion
answers.feedbackHtml: The question concerns usable recovery beyond the copy milestone.

answers.textHtml: Only that the archive is encrypted, without checking key recovery
answers.feedbackHtml: Confidential storage does not establish authorised restore capability.

answers.textHtml: Only that the backup licence is current
answers.feedbackHtml: A licence does not demonstrate restoration of the required service.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Recovery includes data, application dependencies and business usability.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q05
questions.promptHtml: After a payment-system failure, why check whether a file was already sent before retrying?

answers.textHtml: To avoid duplicate or inconsistent business effects
answers.feedbackHtml: A failed response does not necessarily mean the business action did not occur.

answers.textHtml: To assume that a timeout always means the external action did not happen
answers.feedbackHtml: A response can be lost after an external effect.

answers.textHtml: To replace the original payment identity with a new one before checking
answers.feedbackHtml: A new identity can make duplicate effects harder to reconcile.

answers.textHtml: To treat successful server restart as proof of the payment state
answers.feedbackHtml: System availability does not determine the original transaction's effect.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A failed response does not necessarily mean the business action did not occur.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q06
questions.promptHtml: A supplier engineer no longer supports a service. What should happen to access?

answers.textHtml: Review and remove it through the authorised process
answers.feedbackHtml: Access follows current authorised purpose.

answers.textHtml: Retain it because the engineer is skilled
answers.feedbackHtml: Skill is not continuing need.

answers.textHtml: Transfer it to an unnamed shared account
answers.feedbackHtml: That loses personal accountability.

answers.textHtml: Ignore it until the supplier asks
answers.feedbackHtml: The department needs current access control.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Access follows current authorised purpose.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which elements belong in a supplier access record? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Approver, permitted scope and expiry
answers.feedbackHtml: These define authority.

answers.textHtml: Named identity and examinable activity
answers.feedbackHtml: These support accountability.

answers.textHtml: A permanent blank approval
answers.feedbackHtml: It does not bound access.

answers.textHtml: A claim that outsourcing removes departmental responsibility
answers.feedbackHtml: It does not.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Supplier access must remain connected to the service and its owner.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which actions strengthen post-change review? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Verify the actual service outcome
answers.feedbackHtml: The technical change should support the business result.

answers.textHtml: Reconcile transactions around the disruption
answers.feedbackHtml: This identifies duplicate or incomplete effects.

answers.textHtml: Rewrite history to show approval before it existed
answers.feedbackHtml: That destroys trustworthy records.

answers.textHtml: Close all related findings without checking
answers.feedbackHtml: Underlying causes may remain.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Use the actual timeline and service evidence.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q09
questions.promptHtml: A failed-login alert alone proves that the named account holder acted maliciously.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. The alert requires assessment; credential misuse or ordinary error may be involved.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: The alert requires assessment; credential misuse or ordinary error may be involved.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The alert requires assessment; credential misuse or ordinary error may be involved.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q10
questions.promptHtml: An emergency control should have an owner and a route back to a sustainable operating arrangement.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Otherwise the emergency workaround can persist without review.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Otherwise the emergency workaround can persist without review.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Otherwise the emergency workaround can persist without review.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match each event to the needed control focus.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Different events require different operating actions.

questions.name: M03-U02-Q12
questions.promptHtml: Before rerunning a payment action, reconcile its actual [[1]] and possible [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A retry decision needs the original business state.
